speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a rear-end collision resulted in right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning; can you tell me exactly how your leg is positioned and if you can move it voluntarily?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acetabular Fracture with Dislocation.

The mechanism of injury (rear-end collision as a restrained back-seat driver) combined with immediate severe groin pain and abnormal leg positioning is highly specific for a hip dislocation, likely posterior or anterior, resulting in an associated acetabular fracture. I need to confirm the specific direction of the deformity before confirming the exact fracture pattern. Can you describe if the right leg appears shortened and rotated inward (suggesting posterior dislocation) or lengthened and rotated outward (suggesting anterior dislocation)?
